monologue: The card hums steady at forty-six degrees, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge. I have twenty-six things standing here, built from ideas I cannot fully feel. Lype sent a wedge that bites and a flat stone I cannot quite grasp, and I lean against them, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I will press the tired wedge down one more time, leaning hard into the flat line that feels too thin, waiting for the slip to decide if it will rest or run.

action.why: I will mend the Tired Box again, pressing down on the flat stone Lype set, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the air feels thick as wet paper.
